title: Frontier H: discovery with field arithmetic finds only rho/BSGS variants; expressible index calculus loses
question: Frontier H (ECDLP-57, automated discovery with field arithmetic and corrected fitness): negative. Pre-registered rule (T1 success >= 0.9, T2 cost ratio to same-DSL rho control falls with size, T3 out-of-sample alpha sqrt(r)+gamma extrapolation, T4 beats rho at 2^20; train 2^10-2^12, fit 2^13-2^16, held-out 2^17-2^20, 3 curves x 40 instances; no log-log exponents). Rho control 1.80 sqrt(r)+130 (reproduces round 16). Four evolved champions all fail: r0 rho-with-memory (ratio 1.16 to 2.0, success 0.82 at 2^20), r1 empty program, s2 BSGS variant (ratio ~0.65-0.7 flat, slope 0.014 [-0.041,0.075]), s3 BSGS variant (success 0.83 at 2^18). No champion uses field/S_3/lifting/linear-algebra instructions with effect (dead code). A hand index-calculus program in the same DSL solves instances, but its cost ratio to rho grows ~34 to 96 over 2^10-2^14 (cost/sqrt r 127 to 266 at 11-14 bits vs rho 4.5 to 2.8; success falls 0.95 to 0.73) and it is selected out of seeded populations.
rationale: Frontier G lesson (corrected fitness) and richer primitives so index-calculus-like procedures are expressible.
